A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FFOLayer research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original training-loss and runtime experiments on synthetic decision-focused learning and Sudoku in Sections 6–7 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on synthetic decision-focused learning, Sudoku and SOCP, plus scaling, memory, gradient-accuracy and sensitivity experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: Both versions use the active-set Lagrangian surrogate, original and perturbed solves, finite-difference hypergradients and detached-gradient linearization. The solver-agnostic framing and simplification using zero unperturbed ghost multipliers clarify this existing procedure rather than introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 retains synthetic QP decision-focused learning and 9×9 Sudoku, and adds an SOCP task with a nonlinear norm constraint in Section 6.3. This substantially extends empirical coverage beyond linear constraints to the general-convex setting central to the paper.

E2.justification: BPQP and dQP become evaluated comparators in the retained QP/Sudoku experiments, alongside CvxpyLayer, QPTH and LPGD (v2 Figures 3–4). Alt-Diff appears in the conceptual comparison table but is explicitly excluded from reported experiments, so it is not counted as an added empirical baseline.

E3.justification: v1 reports primary LPGD results with tolerance 10^-12; v2 Section 7 instead reports matching the proposed method's tolerance, with the tightened setting examined separately in Figure 8. v2 also introduces dimension, batch-size and tolerance sweeps, CPU/GPU comparisons, and memory, gradient-error and throughput measurements.

E4.justification: v2 adds extensive analyses of problem-size scaling, memory components, approximate-gradient fidelity, batch efficiency, backward-solver tolerance and GPU alternatives (Figures 5–13). Figure 8 also expands v1's qualitative LPGD tolerance observation into a direct loss/runtime comparison.

E5.justification: Appendix G.1 newly states that each experiment uses ten random seeds, and Section 7 describes averaged timings; v1 specifies no run count. Neither version defines confidence intervals or significance tests. This is newly disclosed replication, not evidence that the number of runs increased.

E6.justification: The retained loss/runtime plots are revised, including LPGD results under a reported tolerance change. v2 adds SOCP, BPQP/dQP and diagnostic results, including nearly flat reported FFOCP memory versus sharply increasing CvxpyLayer memory in Figure 6. These are new or revised outcomes, not established same-setting performance gains across versions.

T1.justification: v2 qualifies active-set equivalence with differentiability and local active-set constancy (Theorem 4.5). Lemmas C.1 and E.1 add explicit finite-perturbation error derivations and their detached-gradient counterpart under regularity assumptions. v1 already claimed finite accuracy but relied on cited bounds and an asymptotic argument in Appendix D.2. The principal complexity, general-convex and smoothing results are retained.

C1.justification: The central first-order oracle, convergence-rate and drop-in-library contributions remain. v2 changes the highlighted interface property from objective-agnostic to solver-agnostic, and adds prominent abstract/conclusion claims of comparable convergence with improved runtime and memory scalability. The principal asymptotic rate is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations involving canonicalization overhead, ill-conditioned KKT systems, tolerance stability, memory growth and batch overhead. It replaces v1's specific explanation for improved Sudoku loss with broader robustness/scaling interpretations. Appendix G also qualifies GPU advantages as task-dependent and identifies CvxpyLayer gradients as a proxy reference.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents solver backends, 2,048 synthetic samples with an 80/20 split, two-layer MLPs, Adam, dimensions, tolerances and an eight-core/384-GB allocation. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously unspecified settings. The earlier big-M/DPP implementation explanation is removed, and the code link changes from guaguakai/FFOLayer to GT-KOALA/FFOLayer.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the new Table 1 substantially expand positioning against differentiable optimization layers, especially dQP, BPQP, LPGD and Alt-Diff, and claim a distinctive combination of solver independence, first-order information and finite-time guarantees. Additional differentiable-QP and software-framework references are introduced. The older nonconvex-bilevel survey is largely retained and relocated.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, problem statement and method exposition, restructures Section 4 and refocuses Section 5. Proofs and general-convex discussion move into reorganized appendices, while a conclusion, acknowledgements, impact statement and dedicated experimental appendix reshape the document.

P2.justification: The main text changes to a two-column layout. v2 adds a method illustration and comparison table, redraws the main experiment plots with additional methods and three task panels, and introduces numerous diagnostic figures. The original code example is retained as Figure 2 rather than removed.

improvement.justification: v1's scalability and general-convex claims had only two linearly constrained empirical demonstrations. v2 adds nonlinear SOCP evaluation, stronger comparators and controlled scaling, gradient-accuracy, tolerance and GPU studies, substantially strengthening the empirical basis and exposing tradeoffs. Clearer theorem conditions and experimental disclosures also help. Removed big-M documentation and inconsistent CPU/GPU memory labeling limit reproducibility, but do not outweigh these substantial gains.
